taxonomic_note: Kew POWO and FNA accept Crataegus texana at species level; distinguish from Crataegus mollis sensu stricto, from C. brazoria and from Crataegus viridis. FNA provisionally treats this as a pink/purple-anthered complex containing var. texana and var. dasyphylla. Avoid unverified assignment to variety from one photograph.

field_group: Thorny small tree / shrub with lobed downy leaves and red haws
look_here_first: EXAMINE FOUR THINGS IN THIS ORDER: (1) alternate simple leaves 4–7 cm, often 1–4 LOBES on each side and strong teeth; (2) woolly/white-hairy NEW twigs and flower cups; (3) 20 stamens whose ANTHERS are ROSE–PURPLE (not cream) in open white flower; (4) red pome 9–14 mm usually, 4–5 hard stones. Thorns may be present or absent, so never key this species on a thorn alone.
project_tracker_diagnostic: FNA C. texana: lobed elliptic to rhombic leaves 4–7 cm, young white tomentum, woody straight twig thorns about 4–5 cm when present, corymbs of 7–12 white flowers 14–22 mm wide, stamens 20 with rose to purple anthers, 4–5 styles, red pomes usually 9–14 mm, 4–5 pyrenes.

project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO/FNA establish a native taxon in Texas, Oklahoma/Arkansas/Missouri, but no three independently sourced native occurrences in project's specific 24 Texas counties have been verified in this pass. Williamson County modern photo outside target zone; herbarium cultivated/historical images cannot prove wild county occurrence. Do not promote to confirmed target native metrics.

morphology_keys.habit: Deciduous shrub/small tree, up to about 10 m in FNA broad description, often shorter. Rough fissured gray-brown bark and woody determinate thorns may occur.
morphology_keys.twigs_thorns: Newest twig growth woolly (lanate) and older pale gray to tan. Straight woody twigs thorns absent to frequent, often 4–5 cm on two-year-old stems; may turn chestnut brown or black.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Alternate SIMPLE leaves on woody shoots, not opposite; 4–7 cm broad elliptic to rhombic-ovate, basal margin less toothed, distal margin strongly serrate; 1–4 lobes per side. Tip and lobe depth variable, hairier underside when young.
morphology_keys.leaf_variety_warning: FNA var. texana typically 2–4 deep lobes per side; var. dasyphylla more often 1–2(–3) shallow lobes. Do not claim exact variety from one leaf photograph.
morphology_keys.flower_clusters: Usually 7–12 flowers per broad, somewhat flat cluster; white 5-petaled flowers ~14–22 mm across, flower cup/hypanthium downy-hairy.
morphology_keys.stamens_anthers: About 20 stamens; anthers rose/rose-purple, red or purple. The colored anther is a KEY character in contrast to ivory/cream on C. mollis and usually C. viridis. Confirm before anthers shed pollen or darken/dry.
morphology_keys.styles: 4 or 5 styles, often delicate at flower center. Requires macro; not reliably countable in general flower photo.
morphology_keys.fruit: Red or orange-red miniature apple-like pome, usually 9–14 mm diameter, sometimes to 25 mm, with 4–5 hard inner pyrenes. Fruit COLOR alone not diagnostic.
morphology_keys.habitat: Rich bottomlands or river bottoms, alluvial rich soils and open woodland/brush margins; often near water and in southeastern/central Texas broad regional references. Do not infer local Hays nativity from habitat.
best_field_traits: 4–7 cm lobed and strongly toothed alternate leaves
woolly new twigs / downy flower cups
woody lateral thorns often 4–5 cm but variably absent

comparisons.key_distinctions: Green hawthorn C. viridis: generally smaller 5–8 mm pomes, mostly ivory/cream anthers and often hairless flower cup/branchlets, whereas texana larger hairy cups and pink/purple anthers. Downy hawthorn C. mollis also very hairy but typically ivory/cream anthers. Brazos hawthorn C. brazoria has similarly rose anthers, 20 stamens and red fruit but leaves often elliptic with NO substantial lobes (fruit color may also vary). Mexican plum has white petals but one central stone in a DRUPE, not a multi-stone pome; flowering and thorn architecture differ.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: Texas Hawthorn — four body parts in four photos
photo_diagnostic_lesson.look_here_first: 1. LEAF lobes/teeth; 2. twig and calyx hairs; 3. pink/purple anthers with ~20 stamens; 4. red multi-stone haw fruit.

steps.find: Alternate 4–7 cm toothed blade with 1–4 lobes per side; hair especially along undersurface veins. Count a range, do not call 0-lobed Brazos leaf the same.
Young woolly twig; long straight woody thorn (a modified branch, not an easily peeled off prickle); thorn may be absent.
White 5 petals, look for ~20 stamens and pink-to-purple anthers; count 4–5 styles if an actual macro makes them visible.
A mature red/orange-red pome usually ~9–14 mm with 4–5 bony pyrenes; needs real contemporary fruit dissection photo in final pass.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: TEXANA = LOBED leaves + DOWNY green parts + PINK anthers + RED HAW with 4–5 STONES.

glossary.anther: AN-ther — the pollen-bearing tip of each stamen; color helps distinguish hawthorn species
glossary.stamen: STAY-men — pollen-producing flower organ made of filament plus anther
glossary.style: STILE — slender female column connecting ovary and stigma
glossary.pome: POHM — apple-like fruit derived partly from floral cup tissue
glossary.pyrene: PIE-reen — one hard stone-like structure enclosing seed(s) inside a haw
glossary.tomentum: toh-MEN-tum — woolly coating of short hairs
glossary.thorn: Hard sharp modified stem/branch; not a superficially attached epidermal prickle

items.label: LIVE LEAF · SHAPE AND TOOTHED EDGE
items.creator: iNaturalist photo 209023977; creator/licensing requires per-photo review
items.caption: Study a broad green alternate leaf. Look for 1–4 lobes per side, stronger teeth along margin, and fine hair on young growth. Lobe depth varies by variety; one leaf alone does not prove C. texana.
items.annotation_status: Photo-leaf identity label provisional, rights unresolved; no arbitrary arrows.

items.label: REAL WHITE FLOWER · PINK ANTHERS
items.creator: iNaturalist user pintobeans (photo 187782261); exact photo license not confirmed
items.caption: Williamson County, Texas exact-species observation. Five white petals and about 20 stamens with rose/purple anthers: count and color of ANTHERS are especially useful against cream-anthered downy and green hawthorns. This is NOT Hays native-range evidence.
items.annotation_status: Flower photo provisional rights; count stamens only when individually visible.
